decisions.head: LEAD-ICP-digit-presentation-solving-degree
decisions.source_excerpt:
# H-ECDLP-60de36 -- Does the Petit-Kosters-Messeng 2-isogeny-chain factor base
# (proposed by the user, 2026-10-15, for P-256, where 2^96 | p+1) make Semaev
# m-decomposition cheaper to solve than the same set encoded densely, a random
# set of the same size, or enumeration?  Toy-scale, prime-field, falsifiable.
hypothesis:
  id: H-ECDLP-60de36
  question_id: RQ-ECDLP-001
  experiment_id: EXP-ECDLP-f49f75
  goal_id: GOAL-ECDLP-001
  specified_at: '2026-10-15'
  proposed_by: coordinator
  source: >-
    User proposal in session 2026-10-15: factor base B = {(u,v) in E(F_p) :
    Phi_x(u) = x(Phi(R))} with Phi a chain of 44 Velu 2-isogenies from
    E0: y^2 = x^3 + x (p = 3 mod 4, #E0 = p+1), |B| ~ N^(1/6), decomposition
    T = P1 + ... + P6 via Semaev summation polynomials. The user stated that the
    fast solver is missing; this hypothesis tests whether the chain encoding
    supplies any solver advantage at toy scale.
  title: >-
    Chain-encoded isogeny factor base versus dense encoding of the same set,
    a random set of equal size, and meet-in-the-middle enumeration, for
    Semaev m = 2 and m = 3 decomposition under one Groebner instrument
  statement: >-
    For prime p = 3 mod 4 with 2^L | p+1 and target curve y^2 = x^3 - 3x + b,
    encoding the factor-base x-set V = x(R + <K>) by L chained quadratic Velu
    equations per point (arm A) yields Groebner (std/slimgb + fglm) solving
    times for the Semaev m-decomposition system that are LOWER, and grow more
    slowly in |V| = 2^L, than (B) the same V encoded by its degree-2^L minimal
    polynomial, (C) a random set of size 2^L, and (E) meet-in-the-middle
    enumeration over the factor base.
  mechanism: >-
    PKM (PKC 2016) heuristic: a factor base with a low-degree, many-variable
    description (like a vector subspace in binary-field Weil descent) yields
    systems with small degree of regularity, so total Groebner cost could be
    polynomial in log p per decomposition instead of exponential in |V|.
  structural_ingredients:

idea:

  question_id: RQ-ECDLP-002

  status: proposed
  title: 'Replay lever in the PKM tower F4: measure the target-independent share of cost (confirm or kill, one day)'

  supersedes: null
  lineage:
    extends: null
    note: >-
      Not an extension of the SNFS intake (no B/C/D/E route covers it); belongs to the PKM tower oracle line.
      Nearest ledger record IDEA-20260829-fa8235 (F_2 Boolean row-partition ceiling).
  claim: >-
    [proposed] In f4_fp_tower on m=3 N=15, m=3 N=18, m=4 N=12 (two committed targets each) the systems of two targets
    differ only through x_R. (a) [derived from committed equal counts] per-step structure (columns, reducers, pivot
    leads, promoted rows) is identical across targets. (b) [owner, stated before measuring] the target-independent share
    of multiply-adds is below 5 percent, so a Joux-Vitse-style trace replay is at most a stage-level gain and moves no
    exponent. Reported separately: Z = multiply-adds on S-rows that reduce to zero; U_time = wall-time share of symbolic

    selection and zero-reducing rows; it cannot remove the numeric elimination of non-zero residues, whose values depend
    on x_R. So speedup <= 1/(1-U). Optional arm B: for m >= 3 the chain links without x_R (m-2 of m-1) are
    target-independent; seed F4 with their Groebner basis to degree D and compare C_seed/C_full.

    (J*N/c_d)^(1/d), d <= 12, J <= Jmax, c_d <= Clead, balanced digits) and L (LLL on {c : sum c_i m^i = 0 mod N},
    d <= 6, m in an enumerated set). [derived expectation] Flagged: Curve25519 p (d=5), Ed448 p (d=2), P-192 p (d=3),
    P-521 p (J=16, d=5), BN and BLS12-381 primes; not flagged: brainpool, random primes. Audits companion F_p^* and
    F_{p^2}^* DLP risk and hidden-structure detection, NOT ECDLP; a flag describes an integer, not a curve or a key.
  mechanism: >-
    [derived] Class E has at most Jmax*Clead*(2C+1)^d*2^(-n(1-1/d))*O(d) members per n-bit integer (counting bound);
    flag when log2 of that falls below -64 after the union over the census. Class L is the congruence form: lambda_1 of

    g1*x - g0) with g1 > 1 [retrieved, KN-LIT-7635 PDF sec 4]; E and L see g1 = 1, so the power curve over g1 bits

idea:
  id: IDEA-20261024-3c71a9
  question_id: RQ-PEXT-7c3e91
  goal_id: GOAL-PEXT-4a1d6b
  area: PEXT
  added: '2026-10-24'
  status: proposed
  approved_by: null
  proposed_by: idea-generator
  title: >-
    Norm-character law: why the genus-n GHS family at prime n sits on curves with a rational 4-torsion point,
    and where that stops (q mod 4)
  class: mechanism
  claim: >-
    K = F_{q^n}, q odd, n an odd prime, B' = {sigma^a x : a in S} (x in K minus F_q, |S| = 4) the branch
    quadruple of y^2 = c prod (X - e_i). Because chi_K = chi_q o N_{K/F_q}, which 2-torsion points of E lie in
    2E(K) is an F_2-linear function of eps = chi_q(-1), the bits chi_q(N(x - sigma^k x)), k = 1..(n-1)/2, and a
    twist bit u. At n = 5 (four of five conjugates, the genus-5 family): |E(K)[4]| = 8 on EVERY such curve when
    q = 3 mod 4; when q = 1 mod 4, |E(K)[4]| = 4 on exactly one K-twist of each pair and 8 or 16 on the other.
    So v_2(#E(K)) >= 3 is necessary for genus 5 at q = 3 mod 4 and not at q = 1 mod 4. Derived after reading
    the sibling q = 3 data; the q = 1 mod 4 branch and n = 7 are out-of-sample.
  mechanism: >-
    Pair: (R3 Weil-restriction cover of the x-line with F_q-structure tau; Sigma = <sigma>, the orbit shifts).
    Trichotomy: coordinate-dependent (the genus belongs to the structure; the floor is a minimum over structures).
    Lossy-projection test against Sigma: (x, c) -> (eps, sign bits, u) keeps (n+3)/2 bits and discards x; compatible
    because N o sigma = N, so all shifts share the bits (a block system of <sigma>); lossy because ~q^(n-3)
    configurations map to 2^((n+3)/2) values. Kummer step: the Jacobian's 2-torsion roots are c*theta_i with
    theta_1-theta_2 = d14 d23, theta_1-theta_3 = d13 d24, theta_2-theta_3 = d12 d34 (d_ij = e_i - e_j);
    N(d_ik) = c_{k-i}, c_j = N(x - sigma^j x), c_{-j} = -c_j (n odd): two differences are squares up to u, the
    third has class chi(-c_1 c_2). Sanity: |E(K)[4]| = 16 needs mu_4 in K, i.e. eps = +1, as derived.
  novelty_status: unverified
  citations:
    - ref: aburan28/crypto research/ghs_cover_census_n5_20261013/README.md
      provenance: internal
      claim: n = 5 genus 5 only with |E(K)[4]| = 8 (20 of 60, 0 of 21 with 4); class minima by v_2 at q = 3
      verified_by: idea-generator 2026-10-24, README read in /home/user/crypto checkout

idea:
  id: IDEA-20261024-5f08bd
  question_id: RQ-PEXT-7c3e91
  goal_id: GOAL-PEXT-4a1d6b
  area: PEXT
  added: '2026-10-24'
  status: proposed
  approved_by: null
  proposed_by: idea-generator
  title: >-
    General-prime floor lemma: single-orbit genus floor 2^(n-3-e(n)) (n-4) + 1, e(n) from 4-term relations among
    n-th roots of unity, and the characteristic-2 contrast at Mersenne n
  class: mechanism
  claim: >-
    For prime n >= 5 and branch quadruples on one sigma-orbit (r = n), m = #{zeta in mu_n : s_S(zeta) != 0} for the
    4-term polynomial s_S and g = 2^(m-2)(n-4) + 1, so the single-orbit floor is 2^(n-3-e(n))(n-4) + 1, with e(n)
    the largest number of nontrivial zeta in mu_n killed by one s_S (a union of cosets of <2> in Z/n). Newton
    lemma (char 2): four distinct u_j with p_1 = p_3 = 0 have e_1 = e_3 = 0, hence a repeated root; so zeta and
    zeta^3 are never both zeros, and 3 in <2> in (Z/n)^* forces e(n) = 0. Predictions: e = 0 for n = 5, 11, 13,
    19, 23, 29, 37 and 17; e(7) = 3 (g = 7); e(31) = 5 (conjecture, g = 2^23 * 27 + 1). Cross-characteristic: Hess's
    genus 2^t - 2^(t-s1) - 2^(t-s2) + 1 equals n at every Mersenne prime n = 2^t - 1 (s1 = s2 = t); the odd floor at
    n = 31 is ~2^23 * 27. The weight-4 generator, absent in Artin-Schreier form, is the difference.
  mechanism: >-
    Pair: (R3 Weil-restriction cover, branch set on one orbit; Sigma = <sigma>, shifts of Z/n). Trichotomy:
    coordinate-dependent (the pattern S belongs to the structure). Lossy-projection test against Sigma: S -> the
    nonzero set of s_S in mu_n (the cyclic module it generates) discards positions, keeps (m, r); rotation fixes
    the ideal, so the retained part propagates exactly; lossy because 4-sets far outnumber divisors of x^n - 1.
    Equivalent: m* = minimum F_2-rank of a weight-4 circulant of prime order. g = n at r = n only for (n,m) = (5,4),
    (7,3), from 2^(m-2)(n-4) = n-1.
  novelty_status: unverified
  citations:
    - ref: aburan28/crypto research/odd_char_descent_genus3_20261014/REPORT.md
      provenance: internal
      claim: 'minimum genus by exact period n, values 5, 7, 1793, 9217 at n = 5, 7, 11, 13; tabulates n <= 14 only'
      verified_by: idea-generator 2026-10-24, REPORT read

  title: >-
    Isogeny-walk reachability of a floor cover at prime n: a volcano split-count law and a hits-per-class
    exponent n/2 - 3
  class: mechanism
  claim: >-
    K = F_{q^n}, n prime >= 5, E/K ordinary with Frobenius pi, trace t. (a) Exact: the number of K-isomorphism
    classes in the isogeny class with E(K)[2] = (Z/2)^2 is N_split(t) = sum over orders O containing Z[(pi-1)/2]
    of h(O) (up to j in {0,1728} unit weights); it is positive iff 4 divides #E(K); these are the non-floor
    vertices of the K-rational 2-isogeny volcanoes, so every curve of such a class is within one K-rational
    2-isogeny of a split curve. (b) Heuristic scaling: floor-family curves (genus n, about c_n q^(n-3), 10 q^2 at
    n = 5) divided by classes with 4 dividing #E (about q^(n/2)) give lambda_n q^(n/2-3) hits per class: at n = 5
    the share of such classes holding a hit falls like q^(-1/2); at n = 7 it tends to 1. (c) Competing
    explanation: hits are biased by 2-adic shape (IDEA-20261024-3c71a9), so classes with v_2(#E(K)) = 2 hold no
    genus-5 curve at q = 3 mod 4 however large N_split is.
  mechanism: >-
    Pair: (R3 Weil-restriction cover; Sigma = K-rational 2-isogenies, which change the 2-torsion Galois type,
    and odd-degree K-isogenies, which keep E[2] as a Galois module and re-randomise j). Trichotomy: 2-isogenies
    are a partial action (they reach the split locus deterministically along a volcano); odd isogenies are
    branching (they re-draw the configuration; a hit has density ~ q^-3). Lossy-projection test against Sigma:
    E -> (t, volcano level, 2-adic shape of E(K)) discards j and the configuration; compatible because
    Sigma-isogenous curves share t and the level and shape are functions of End(E) (a block system of the
    isogeny graph); lossy because a class holds ~q^(n/2) curves. Mixing of odd-ell walks on Cl(O) is kept
    separate (H2).

decisions.source_excerpt:
idea:
  id: IDEA-20261024-a29e53
  question_id: RQ-PEXT-7c3e91
  goal_id: GOAL-PEXT-4a1d6b
  area: PEXT
  added: '2026-10-24'
  status: proposed
  approved_by: null
  proposed_by: idea-generator
  title: >-
    Is the cover floor the genus floor? Which isogeny classes of Res_{K/F_q}E hold a genus-n Jacobian, exhaustively
    at n = 3 (n = 2 control), and a Torelli-density exponent for general prime n
  class: measurement
  claim: >-
    K = F_{q^n}, E/K ordinary of trace t. The isogeny class of W = Res_{K/F_q}E has L-polynomial 1 - tT^n + Q T^(2n),
    so a genus-n curve C/F_q has Jac(C) isogenous to W iff N_i(C) = q^i + 1 for i < n and N_n = Q + 1 - n t (Tate).
    At n = 3 this is N_1 = q+1, N_2 = q^2+1. Claim: for every class t with irreducible T^6 - tT^3 + Q, the class t or
    its quadratic-twist class -t holds a genus-3 F_q-curve (hyperelliptic or plane quartic), by Torelli plus Serre's
    twist theorem for the simple threefold W; so classes with #E(K) odd or 2 mod 4, where the GHS cover floor is
    13 / 5 (proved), still hold genus-3 Jacobians, and the cover floor is not the genus floor. Existence is not
    descent: a transfer needs an explicit F_q-isogeny J(C) -> W of controlled degree (Tian 2023 gives one family),
    which this idea does not touch. For general prime n, the expected number of genus-n curves per class is
    c_n q^(e(n)), e(n) = (-n^2 + 11n - 12)/4.
  mechanism: >-
    Pair: (R3 Weil restriction W as an abelian variety of dimension n; Sigma = F_q-rational isogenies, of any
    degree). Trichotomy: coordinate-dependent (class membership is intrinsic, the curve C is a choice of
    representative; the GHS cover is the special case with an explicit map). Lossy-projection test against Sigma:
    W -> L-polynomial discards the isomorphism class and keeps the isogeny class; Sigma preserves it exactly (a
    block-system quotient), lossy because a class holds many ppav. Density heuristic: ~q^(3n-3) genus-n curves,
    the n-1 vanishing coefficients c_1..c_(n-1) cost q^(-n(n-1)/4), the value of c_n costs q^(-n/2), giving e(n).
    e = 1.5, 3, 4.5, 4, -3 at n = 2, 3, 5, 7, 11; zero near n = 9.8. The resemblance to Diem's n >= 11 threshold
    for GHS is noted, not claimed (different objects, naive independence).
  novelty_status: unverified
  citations:
    - ref: KN-LIT-b4a89c
      provenance: internal

idea:
  id: IDEA-20261024-d84f20
  question_id: RQ-PEXT-7c3e91
  goal_id: GOAL-PEXT-4a1d6b
  area: PEXT
  added: '2026-10-24'
  status: proposed
  approved_by: null
  proposed_by: idea-generator
  title: >-
    Which branch types can a given E realise? Degree-2 functions beyond x are indexed by E(K)/2E(K), and
    the n = 3 "Type 2" plane-quartic family is expected to be the nontrivial class
  class: mechanism
  claim: >-
    For E/K, K = F_{q^n}, q odd, n prime, the K-rational degree-2 functions are f_T, T in E(K)/2E(K) (|E(K)[2]|
    of them, T = 0 is x), with branch set B_T = f_T({P : 2P = T}), an E[2]-torsor. Its Frobenius cycle type is
    fixed by E[2]/(F-1)E[2]: E(K)[2] = 0 gives only (1,3); Z/2 gives (1,1,2) at T = 0 and a single 4-cycle at
    T != 0; (Z/2)^2 gives (1^4) at T = 0 and (2,2) at T != 0. T != 0 never has a K-rational branch point. In the
    sibling construction the T != 0 genera are: 4-cycle, g in {1, (n-1)2^n+1}; (2,2), g in {1, 2^(n-2)(n-2)+1
    [one shared 2n-orbit, (m,r) = (n-1,2n)], 2^(n-1)(n-1)+1, (n-1)2^n+1}. So the floor over all degree-2
    functions equals the x-line floor for n >= 5 (25 > 5 at n = 5, 161 > 7 at n = 7) and ties it at n = 3, where
    (m,r) = (2,6), a single 6-orbit absent from the x-line, is expected to be the Momose-Chao Type 2 family
    (to be checked).
  mechanism: >-
    Pair: (R3 Weil-restriction cover with F_q-structure tau; operation set Sigma = Frobenius shifts of B_T).
    Trichotomy: coordinate-dependent (choice of degree-2 function plus structure). Lossy-projection test against
    Sigma: E -> (Galois type of the torsor, cycle type of B_T) keeps what the genus depends on (Theorem 1 of the
    odd-characteristic study) and drops j; Sigma-propagation is exact since g is a function of sigma-orbit data.
    Orbit step: for a 4-cycle or (2,2) B_T the tau-orbit of a branch point has size 2^a n or is tau-stable (then
    j in F_q, g = 1, descended); the span is a cyclic module over F_2[x]/((x^n-1)^2), non-semisimple, new to the
    n = 3, 5 studies. Shared orbit: s = (x^n+1)(x^k+1), gcd(x^n+1, x^k+1) = x+1, so m = n-1, r = 2n.
  novelty_status: unverified

      provenance: internal
      claim: '"Not established: degree-2 maps other than x"; census uses B = x(E[2]) and infinity'
